questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you never do?

options.text: Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
Change lanes suddenly without warning.
Check for other vehicles in the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes suddenly without warning.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and blind spots to make sure no other vehicles are there. Always signal before changing lanes. This gives other drivers time to react.

questions.question: You park uphill on a road with no curb. Which way should you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Straight ahead
Right, toward the side of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the side of the road
questions.explanation: When parking uphill or downhill on a road with no curb, turn your wheels away from the center of the road. This way, if your brakes fail, the car will roll away from traffic.

questions.question: A large truck ahead of you is turning right onto a street with two lanes in each direction. What will the truck do?

options.text: Complete its turn in either of the two lanes.
Swing wide to complete the right turn.
Stay in the right lane at all times while turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Swing wide to complete the right turn.
questions.explanation: Large trucks need extra space to turn. The rear wheels follow a shorter path than the front wheels. The longer the vehicle, the wider it must swing to turn safely.

questions.question: Which of these is a safe driving technique?

options.text: Using high beam lights in the fog.
Staring only at the road directly ahead.
Checking your rearview mirrors regularly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Checking your rearview mirrors regularly.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirrors every 2 to 5 seconds to stay aware of hazards. Do not stare at only the road ahead. In fog, use low beam headlights, not high beams.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Side road.
Merge.
Yield the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Side road.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a side road intersects with the road you are on ahead.

questions.question: Who must drivers turning left yield to?

options.text: Oncoming vehicles going straight or turning right.
Passing cars.
No one in particular.

questions.correctAnswerText: Oncoming vehicles going straight or turning right.
questions.explanation: A driver turning left must yield to all vehicles coming from the opposite direction. This includes cars, bicycles, and motorcycles.

questions.question: Which road is most likely to be slippery in cold weather after snow or rain?

options.text: A hilly, open road
A residential road
A road in a shaded area

questions.correctAnswerText: A road in a shaded area
questions.explanation: Shaded spots freeze before other parts of the road and thaw out later. These areas are often icy on cold, wet days.

questions.question: What is the speed limit on a country paved road if no sign is posted?

options.text: 20 mph
30 mph
45 mph

questions.correctAnswerText: 45 mph
questions.explanation: The default speed limit on a country paved road is 45 miles per hour. Always follow posted speed limit signs when they are displayed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Come to a complete stop.
Keep a steady speed while looking and listening for trains.
Slow down, look both ways, listen for trains, and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, look both ways, listen for trains, and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing with this sign, slow down and look both ways. Listen for trains and be prepared to stop if one is coming. Never try to go around a train.

questions.question: When passing another car, when do you have enough space to return to the driving lane?

options.text: When the other driver signals for you to move back.
When you look over your shoulder and see the car behind you.
When you can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: You have enough space to return to the lane when you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. This means there is a safe gap between your car and theirs.

questions.question: What should you do when driving at night?

options.text: Always use your high beams.
Look directly at the headlights of an oncoming vehicle.
Stay farther behind the car in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind the car in front of you.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance at night when it is harder to see. Use your headlights properly, following rules about high and low beams. Do not look directly at oncoming headlights, as the glare can blind you.

questions.question: In which situation should your wheels not point straight ahead?

options.text: When waiting to turn left at a traffic light.
When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.
When parked on a flat road with no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.
questions.explanation: When waiting to turn left, keep your wheels straight. If hit from behind, this prevents you from sliding into oncoming traffic. When parked on a hill, angle your wheels so the car will roll away from traffic if brakes fail.

questions.question: Which factor affects how fast a person absorbs alcohol?

options.text: Weight
Height
Intelligence

questions.correctAnswerText: Weight
questions.explanation: A person's weight affects alcohol absorption. Other factors include biological sex and how much food they have eaten. The only way to remove alcohol from your body is to wait for time to pass.

questions.question: You park facing uphill on a street with a curb. What should you do with your front wheels?

options.text: Turn them toward the curb.
Turn them away from the curb.
Leave them straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn them away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parked facing uphill with a curb, turn wheels away from the curb. When parked uphill with no curb or when parked facing downhill, turn wheels toward the curb or edge.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not enter.
No parking.
No U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn. You cannot turn around to go in the opposite direction at this intersection.

questions.question: When a school bus is picking up or dropping off children, you must:

options.text: Stop no matter which direction you are traveling.
Stop only if you are driving in the same direction.
Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop no matter which direction you are traveling.
questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop before reaching a school bus that is picking up or dropping off children. This applies no matter what direction you are traveling.

questions.question: You reach a four-way stop at the same time as a driver on your left. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver on your left has the right-of-way.
You have the right-of-way.
Whoever is signaling to turn has the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way.

questions.question: You are approaching an intersection with a steady yellow light and have not entered it yet. You should:

options.text: Speed up to cross before the red light.
Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.
Stop safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop safely.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means you should prepare to stop. If you have already entered the intersection, clear it quickly and safely.

questions.question: The first thing that alcohol affects is:

options.text: Vision.
Judgment.
Balance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Judgment.
questions.explanation: Alcohol damages all the abilities you need to drive safely. It goes from your stomach to your blood, then spreads throughout your body. Alcohol first affects the parts of your brain that control judgment and driving skills.

questions.question: After stopping, it is legal to turn left at a red light only if:

options.text: You are on a two-way street turning onto a two-way street.
You are on a one-way street turning onto another one-way street.
You yield to all other traffic at the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are on a one-way street turning onto another one-way street.
questions.explanation: After a complete stop, you can turn left at a red light only if you are on a one-way street and turning onto another one-way street. Make sure no signs prohibit this turn.

questions.question: If another driver is passing you in a no passing zone, you should:

options.text: Pull off the road.
Keep your speed and position the same.
Slow down to let the other driver return to the lane safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to let the other driver return to the lane safely.
questions.explanation: Help the passing vehicle return to the lane easily. This helps everyone avoid danger ahead.

questions.question: Streets and highways are most slippery:

options.text: After it has been raining hard for several hours.
When they are clean and dry.
Right when rain starts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right when rain starts.
questions.explanation: Roads become very slippery in the first half hour of rain. Water mixes with oil and other chemicals on the road that have not washed away yet. Drive with extra care on wet roads.

questions.question: A driver license is a:

options.text: Right, not a privilege.
Privilege, not a right.
Requirement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Privilege, not a right.
questions.explanation: A driver license is a privilege that you must earn and keep. It is not a right.

questions.question: Following a motorcycle too closely is dangerous because:

options.text: Motorcycles do not follow the same rules as other vehicles.
Motorcycles can stop much faster than regular vehicles.
Motorcycles brake more slowly than other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles can stop much faster than regular vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles can stop very quickly. If you follow too closely and the motorcyclist makes a mistake, you won't have enough time or space to avoid a crash.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should:

options.text: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
Slow down and use your high beam headlights.
Turn your lights on and off to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In fog, slow down and use your low beam headlights. If the fog is too thick to see, pull off the road and wait for it to clear.

questions.question: If oncoming headlights are blinding you at night, you should:

options.text: Look toward the right edge of the road.
Switch to your high beams.
Turn your lights on and off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: When blinded by oncoming headlights, look at the right edge of the road instead of straight ahead. This keeps your vehicle on the road safely until you pass the other car.

questions.question: You want to park downhill on a two-way road with no curb. Which way should you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Straight ahead
Right, toward the side of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the side of the road
questions.explanation: When parking downhill on a road without a curb, turn your wheels right toward the road edge. This way your car will roll away from traffic if the brakes fail. When parking uphill without a curb, turn your wheels left toward the center so the car rolls into the curb if brakes fail.

questions.question: If a tire blows out while driving, you should:

options.text: Press the brake hard and hold it.
Hold the wheel tightly and use the brakes gently.
Pull over quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the wheel tightly and use the brakes gently.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel tight and keep the car straight. Slow down gradually by easing off the gas and using the brakes lightly. If possible, pull off the road in a safe place instead of stopping on the road.

questions.question: To avoid hydroplaning in rain, you should:

options.text: Drive at the speed you would in dry conditions.
Brake as soon as your car starts to skid.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your tires lose contact with the road and ride on top of water. It occurs when you drive too fast in wet conditions. Slow down when it rains to prevent this dangerous situation.

questions.question: Which road surface freezes first?

options.text: A tunnel
An intersection
A bridge

questions.correctAnswerText: A bridge
questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before surrounding roads and thaw after them. This is because bridges lose heat from both above and below, making them colder than regular pavement.
